120	Remember I said that the word "this day" is mentioned here
121	once, and also here: "and HaShem has declared you this day."
122	So let's start with the Ramban, who begins by explaining "this day":
123	"And HaShem has declared this day" — for this day is for you like the day of
124	Sinai,
125	like the day of Sinai, and HaShem exalted and raised you through receiving
126	the Torah, to be for Him a treasured people above all peoples, for only
127	you received the Torah.
128	So there is a correspondence between these two days: the day of
129	the giving of the Torah at Mount Sinai and this day.
130	I'll try briefly to repeat something we spoke
131	about in the past, in Parashat Bechukotai,
132	and in previous years also here in Parashat Ki Tavo. A very
133	important point.
134	At Mount Sinai
135	we will see in a moment the verses describing
136	the scene at Mount Sinai, or what happened before the giving of the Torah,
137	the Holy One, blessed be He, offers us the Torah through
138	Moshe Rabbeinu,
139	and we said "we will do and we will hear," and we meant it.
140	But as is known, 40 days after the giving of the Torah
141	came the sin of the golden calf,
142	and we did not receive the Torah, that is, we did not receive
143	it in practice; the tablets were broken on the 17th of Tammuz.
144	Now there were two covenants: there was a covenant sealed
145	at Sinai
146	and another covenant at the end of the 40 years, in the Plains of Moav,
147	in the continuation of this parashah, Parashat Ki Tavo. In fact,
148	this is the heart of Parashat Ki Tavo, but since
149	we spoke about it in previous years, I won't repeat
150	it now. The heart of the parashah is the rebuke,
151	the section of the rebuke, right: if you listen to His commandments,
152	it will be so, and if you do not listen, it will be otherwise. And it is written
153	there at the end:
154	"These are the words of the covenant that HaShem commanded Moshe to make with the children of Israel
155	in the land of Moav, besides the covenant He made with them
156	at Horev." So there were two covenants, and the question is why two
157	covenants are needed. The answer, as we said: the first covenant
158	was broken.
